answer: Trace-Bound Attestation. Each agent action emits a signed record chained to its full prior history hash, so identity is the trajectory, not a key. A clone must replay a distinct, coherent history whose sparrow-like rarity resists copying. Verification compares trajectory depth against a rotating zenith threshold. Attackers pay by fabricating entire histories with unique pigment patterns, costing compute and time per identity, while reuse collapses instantly.
